claim: Cardiac repolarization is determined in part by the slow delayed rectifier current (IKs), through the tetrameric voltage-gated ion channel, KCNQ1, and its β-subunit, KCNE1.
source: Cardiac repolarization is determined in part by the slow delayed rectifier current (IKs), through the tetrameric voltage-gated ion channel, KCNQ1, and its β-subunit, KCNE1.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of cardiac electrophysiology.

claim: The stoichiometry between α and β-subunits has been controversial with studies reporting either a strict 2 KCNE1:4 KCNQ1 or a variable ratio up to 4:4.
source: The stoichiometry between α and β-subunits has been controversial with studies reporting either a strict 2 KCNE1:4 KCNQ1 or a variable ratio up to 4:4.
evidence: This summarizes the state of the literature on the topic.

claim: EQQ and EQQQQ have increasingly hyperpolarized activation compared to EQ.
source: Whole cell and single-channel recordings showed EQQ and EQQQQ to have increasingly hyperpolarized activation, reduced conductance, and shorter first latency of opening compared to EQ - all abolished by the addition of KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from whole cell and single-channel recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: EQQ and EQQQQ have reduced conductance compared to EQ.
source: Whole cell and single-channel recordings showed EQQ and EQQQQ to have increasingly hyperpolarized activation, reduced conductance, and shorter first latency of opening compared to EQ - all abolished by the addition of KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from whole cell and single-channel recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: EQQ and EQQQQ have shorter first latency of opening compared to EQ.
source: Whole cell and single-channel recordings showed EQQ and EQQQQ to have increasingly hyperpolarized activation, reduced conductance, and shorter first latency of opening compared to EQ - all abolished by the addition of KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from whole cell and single-channel recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: The differences in activation, conductance, and first latency between EQQ/EQQQQ and EQ are abolished by the addition of KCNE1.
source: Whole cell and single-channel recordings showed EQQ and EQQQQ to have increasingly hyperpolarized activation, reduced conductance, and shorter first latency of opening compared to EQ - all abolished by the addition of KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from whole cell and single-channel recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: EQQQQ and EQQ crosslinking rates are progressively slowed compared to KCNQ1.
source: As well, using a UV-crosslinking unnatural amino acid in KCNE1, we found EQQQQ and EQQ crosslinking rates to be progressively slowed compared to KCNQ1, which demonstrates that no intrinsic mechanism limits the association of up to four β-subunits within the IKs complex.
evidence: This is supported by UV-crosslinking experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: No intrinsic mechanism limits the association of up to four β-subunits within the IKs complex.
source: As well, using a UV-crosslinking unnatural amino acid in KCNE1, we found EQQQQ and EQQ crosslinking rates to be progressively slowed compared to KCNQ1, which demonstrates that no intrinsic mechanism limits the association of up to four β-subunits within the IKs complex.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the UV-crosslinking experimental data.

claim: KCNQ1 and KCNE1 together conduct the slow delayed rectifier current (IKs) in the heart.
source: In the heart, KCNQ1 and KCNE1 together conduct the slow delayed rectifier current (IKs).
evidence: This is established knowledge in cardiac electrophysiology.

claim: IKs current is primarily responsible for stabilizing repolarization and shortening action potential duration at high heart rates.
source: This current is primarily responsible for stabilizing repolarization and shortening action potential duration at high heart rates (Marx et al., 2002; Ackerman, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Several inherited mutations in KCNQ1 or KCNE1 result in life-threatening arrhythmogenic syndromes including long QT types 1 and 5, short QT type 2, or familial atrial fibrillation.
source: Several inherited mutations in KCNQ1 or KCNE1 result in the life-threating arrhythmogenic syndromes long QT (LQT) types 1 and 5, short QT type 2 or familial atrial fibrillation (Splawski et al., 2000;Bellocq et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: KCNQ1 and KCNE1 are involved in hearing, where mutations have been linked with Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome.
source: In addition to their role in the heart, KCNQ1 and KCNE1 are also involved in hearing, where mutations have been linked with Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome, an inherited form of LQT syndrome accompanied by deafness (Jervell and Lange-Nielsen, 1957; Neyroud et al., 1997; Schulze-Bahr et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome is an inherited form of LQT syndrome accompanied by deafness.
source: In addition to their role in the heart, KCNQ1 and KCNE1 are also involved in hearing, where mutations have been linked with Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome, an inherited form of LQT syndrome accompanied by deafness (Jervell and Lange-Nielsen, 1957; Neyroud et al., 1997; Schulze-Bahr et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: KCNQ1 and KCNE1 complexes have been found in the proximal tubule of the kidney, where they participate in secretory transduction.
source: KCNQ1 and KCNE1 complexes have also been found in the proximal tubule of the kidney, where they participate in secretory transduction (Vallon et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: KCNQ1 has a classic six transmembrane domain structure consisting of a voltage sensor domain (VSD; S1-S4) and pore domain (S5-S6), which assemble into a tetrameric channel.
source: KCNQ1 has a classic six transmembrane domain structure consisting of a voltage sensor domain (VSD; S1-S4) and pore domain (S5-S6), which assemble into a tetrameric channel.
evidence: This is established knowledge about KCNQ1 structure.

claim: KCNQ1 has flexible gating characteristics and the association with accessory β-subunits can drastically modulate its gating behavior.
source: Unlike other Kv channels, KCNQ1 has flexible gating characteristics and the association with accessory β-subunits can drastically modulate its gating behavior (Eldstrom and Fedida, 2011; Liin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: KCNE1 is a single transmembrane domain protein proposed to reside in the exterior cleft formed between the voltage sensor domains of the α-subunits.
source: The best characterized of these accessory subunits is KCNE1, a single transmembrane domain protein proposed to reside in the exterior cleft formed between the voltage sensor domains of the α-subunits (Sanguinetti et al., 1996; Barhanin et al., 1996; Osteen et al., 2010; Kang et al., 2008; Van Horn et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The association of KCNE1 has been found to increase channel conductance, remove inactivation, and depolarize the voltage dependence of activation.
source: The association of KCNE1 has been found to increase channel conductance, remove inactivation, and depolarize the voltage dependence of activation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Several studies have reported a ratio of two β-subunits to every four α-subunits.
source: Since the identification of the components that comprise this channel almost 20 years ago, several studies have reported a ratio of two β-subunits to every four α-subunits (Kang et al., 2008; Wang and Goldstein, 1995; Chen et al., 2003; Morin and Kobertz, 2007; Morin and Kobertz, 2008; Plant et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Other experiments have suggested a more flexible stoichiometry with anywhere from one to four β-subunits associating per KCNQ1 tetramer depending on their concentration.
source: However, other experiments have suggested a more flexible stoichiometry with anywhere from one to four β-subunits associating per KCNQ1 tetramer depending on their concentration (Yu et al., 2013; Cui et al., 1994; Wang, 1998; Morokuma et al., 2008; Zheng et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2011; Strutz-Seebohm et al., 2011; Nakajo et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Nakajo and colleagues characterized a flexible stoichiometry up to 4:4 that was dependent on the relative density of KCNE1 in the membrane.
source: Working in oocytes, Nakajo and colleagues characterized a flexible stoichiometry up to 4:4 that was dependent on the relative density of KCNE1 in the membrane (Nakajo et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Plant et al. (2014) reported that KCNQ1 tetramers were only present on the cell surface in a 2:4 or 0:4 stoichiometry with KCNE1.
source: Using a similar approach in mammalian cells, Plant et al. (2014) reported that KCNQ1 tetramers were only present on the cell surface in a 2:4 or 0:4 stoichiometry with KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Plant et al. (2014) found that the 2:4 ratio was not exceeded even in the presence of increasing KCNE1 concentrations.
source: They also found that the 2:4 ratio was not exceeded even in the presence of increasing KCNE1 concentrations.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The observation of a maximum of 2 KCNE1 subunits per tetramer suggests an intrinsic cooperative mechanism preventing the association of a third or fourth β-subunit during channel assembly.
source: Their observation of a maximum of 2 KCNE1 subunits per tetramer suggests an intrinsic cooperative mechanism preventing the association of a third or fourth β-subunit during channel assembly.
evidence: This is an inference from the Plant et al. (2014) study.

claim: All four of KCNQ1's exterior clefts are accessible to KCNE1.
source: In each instance, we were able to demonstrate that all four of KCNQ1's exterior clefts are accessible to KCNE1, confirming the variable stoichiometry model for channel complex assembly.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fusion proteins, single-channel recordings, and UV-crosslinking experiments.

claim: A 4:4 stoichiometry of KCNQ1 to KCNE1 maximizes channel conductance.
source: In addition, the single channel analysis suggests that a 4:4 stoichiometry of KCNQ1 to KCNE1 maximizes channel conductance.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: KCNQ1 expressed alone had a V1/2 of -15.5 mV.
source: As is known, KCNQ1 expressed alone had a V1/2 of -15.5 mV, while the presence of additional tethered β-subunits resulted in a progressive depolarization of the V1/2 of activation to a maximum of ~+30 mV, (Figure 1E and H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The presence of additional tethered β-subunits resulted in a progressive depolarization of the V1/2 of activation to a maximum of ~+30 mV.
source: As is known, KCNQ1 expressed alone had a V1/2 of -15.5 mV, while the presence of additional tethered β-subunits resulted in a progressive depolarization of the V1/2 of activation to a maximum of ~+30 mV, (Figure 1E and H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The linked subunits contribute to channel complex regulation.
source: This indicates that the linked subunits contribute to channel complex regulation.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed changes in V1/2 with different fusion constructs.

claim: In the presence of excess additional β-subunits, all the α-subunit complex configurations had V1/2's equivalent to that of EQ.
source: In the presence of excess additional β-subunits, all the α-subunit complex configurations had V1/2's equivalent to that of EQ (Figure 1F and H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The convergence of the V1/2's of activation to ~+30 mV suggests that the independent GFP-tagged β-subunits can participate in channel gating.
source: This convergence of the V1/2's of activation to ~+30 mV, particularly the depolarizing shift of EQQQQ and EQQ, suggests that the independent GFP-tagged β-subunits can participate in channel gating.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed convergence of V1/2 values.

claim: EQ 4:4 complexes open after a variable delay period and show fairly consistent bursts of opening that are close to 0.5 pA in amplitude.
source: The EQ 4:4 complexes open after a variable delay period and show fairly consistent bursts of opening that are close to 0.5 pA in amplitude.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel recording data shown in Figure 2.

claim: EQQ and EQQQQ channels open to lower levels than the EQ channels.
source: In comparison, it can be seen that EQQ and EQQQQ channels open to lower levels than the EQ channels.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel recording data shown in Figure 2.

claim: EQQ channels show extremely long residence times in lower sublevels and rarely reach the fully open amplitudes seen in the EQ tracings.
source: In fact, EQQ channels show extremely long residence times in lower sublevels and rarely, or in the case of EQQQQ never, reach the fully open amplitudes seen in the EQ tracings.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel recording data shown in Figure 2.

claim: EQQQQ channels never reach the fully open amplitudes seen in the EQ tracings.
source: In fact, EQQ channels show extremely long residence times in lower sublevels and rarely, or in the case of EQQQQ never, reach the fully open amplitudes seen in the EQ tracings.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel recording data shown in Figure 2.

claim: For EQ, the peak of the events amplitude histogram is at ~0.45 pA.
source: While for EQ it can be seen that the peak of the events amplitude histogram is at ~0.45 pA, it is only 0.18 pA for EQQ, and barely separable from the closed events distribution in the case of EQQQQ, despite very large numbers of events.
evidence: This is supported by amplitude histogram data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: For EQQ, the peak of the events amplitude histogram is at 0.18 pA.
source: While for EQ it can be seen that the peak of the events amplitude histogram is at ~0.45 pA, it is only 0.18 pA for EQQ, and barely separable from the closed events distribution in the case of EQQQQ, despite very large numbers of events.
evidence: This is supported by amplitude histogram data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: For EQQQQ, the peak of the events amplitude histogram is barely separable from the closed events distribution.
source: While for EQ it can be seen that the peak of the events amplitude histogram is at ~0.45 pA, it is only 0.18 pA for EQQ, and barely separable from the closed events distribution in the case of EQQQQ, despite very large numbers of events.
evidence: This is supported by amplitude histogram data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Werry et al. (2013) observed a slope conductance of 3.2 pS from separately co-expressed KCNQ1 and KCNE1.
source: The dotted line in the plotted current-voltage relationships (Figure 2C) refers to a slope conductance of 3.2 pS observed by Werry et al. (2013) from separately co-expressed KCNQ1 and KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The data from the EQ construct overlay the prior published data, and the fit line gives a mean slope conductance of 3.0 pS.
source: Clearly, the data from the EQ construct overlay the prior published data, and the fit line gives a mean slope conductance of 3.0 pS.
evidence: This is supported by current-voltage relationship data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: For EQQ, the mean conductance data gives a value of only 1.3 pS, well below that observed for KCNE1 and KCNQ1 co-expressed separately.
source: However, for EQQ, the mean conductance data gives a value of only 1.3 pS, well below that observed for KCNE1 and KCNQ1 co-expressed separately (Figure 3C) or as EQ together (p<0.01).
evidence: This is supported by current-voltage relationship data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Due to the small amplitudes and brevity of EQQQQ openings it was not possible to derive a conductance value.
source: Due to the small amplitudes and brevity of EQQQQ openings it was not possible to derive a conductance value.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the data analysis.

claim: EQ observed the same five sublevels described before for E1 and Q1 expressed separately, plus an additional sixth smaller opening level at 0.08 pA.
source: In EQ we observed the same five sublevels described before for E1 and Q1 expressed separately, plus an additional sixth smaller opening level at 0.08 pA that we did not see as clearly before.
evidence: This is supported by subconductance analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: EQ had its longest open residency in the second highest sublevel at 0.44 pA (36% of the time spent open).
source: Again, EQ had its longest open residency in the second highest sublevel at 0.44 pA (36% of the time spent open), and split its remaining open time fairly evenly across the other sublevels.
evidence: This is supported by subconductance analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: EQQ visited the same subconductance levels as EQ, but spent most of its time at the lower levels.
source: EQQ visited the same subconductance levels, but spent most of its time at the lower levels, only reaching the 0.44 pA level for 0.6% of the time it spent open.
evidence: This is supported by subconductance analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The most commonly occupied subconductance state for EQQ was the 0.29 pA sublevel, which it occupied 34% of the total open time.
source: The most commonly occupied subconductance state for EQQ was the 0.29 pA sublevel, which it occupied 34% of the total open time.
evidence: This is supported by subconductance analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The open pore architecture of the IKs channel complex is not altered by the presence of only two E1 subunits in EQQ.
source: The data suggest that the open pore architecture of the IKs, channel complex is not altered by the presence of only two E1 subunits in EQQ, just that the stability of higher subconductance levels is reduced to such an extent that their occupancy becomes probabilistically unlikely.
evidence: This is an inference from the subconductance analysis data.

claim: The stability of higher subconductance levels is reduced in EQQ to such an extent that their occupancy becomes probabilistically unlikely.
source: The data suggest that the open pore architecture of the IKs, channel complex is not altered by the presence of only two E1 subunits in EQQ, just that the stability of higher subconductance levels is reduced to such an extent that their occupancy becomes probabilistically unlikely.
evidence: This is an inference from the subconductance analysis data.

claim: The first latency to opening of single channels was reduced for EQQ compared with EQ, from 1.48 ± 0.18 s to 0.94 ± 0.07 s (p<0.05).
source: Consistent with more rapid activation of the EQQ and EQQQQ channel complexes, the first latency to opening of single channels was reduced compared with EQ, from 1.48 ± 0.18 s to 0.94 ± 0.07 s (p<0.05), and to 0.81 ± 0.07 s (p<0.01), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Table 1.

claim: The first latency to opening of single channels was reduced for EQQQQ compared with EQ, from 1.48 ± 0.18 s to 0.81 ± 0.07 s (p<0.01).
source: Consistent with more rapid activation of the EQQ and EQQQQ channel complexes, the first latency to opening of single channels was reduced compared with EQ, from 1.48 ± 0.18 s to 0.94 ± 0.07 s (p<0.05), and to 0.81 ± 0.07 s (p<0.01), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Table 1.

claim: Independently-expressed KCNE1 and KCNQ1 shows a mean first latency of 1.50 ± 0.12 s.
source: These numbers may be compared with independently-expressed KCNE1 and KCNQ1, which shows a mean first latency of 1.50 ± 0.12 s (Werry et al., 2013) and (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Table 1 and a citation to prior research.

claim: It was possible to increase the amplitude of EQQ and EQQQQ construct channel openings by co-expressing them with additional KCNE1.
source: Interestingly, it was possible to increase the amplitude of EQQ and EQQQQ construct channel openings and delay their first latency to opening by co-expressing them with additional KCNE1 (Figure 3, and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: It was possible to delay the first latency to opening of EQQ and EQQQQ construct channels by co-expressing them with additional KCNE1.
source: Interestingly, it was possible to increase the amplitude of EQQ and EQQQQ construct channel openings and delay their first latency to opening by co-expressing them with additional KCNE1 (Figure 3, and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: The current openings of the resulting EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 channel complexes routinely reach 0.4–0.5 pA.
source: These data are shown in a similar format and now it can be clearly seen that the current openings of the resulting EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 channel complexes routinely reach 0.4–0.5 pA, also confirmed by the open events histograms (Figure 3B) and the current-voltage relationships (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The slope of the current-voltage relationships for EQQ+KCNE1 was 3.0 ± 0.18 pS.
source: The slope of the current-voltage relationships for EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 were 3.0 ± 0.18 pS, and 2.9 ± 0.15 pS, respectively, which were not significantly different from KCNQ1 and KCNE1 expressed separately (2.9 ± 0.12 pS; P>0.05).
evidence: This is supported by current-voltage relationship data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The slope of the current-voltage relationships for EQQQQ+KCNE1 was 2.9 ± 0.15 pS.
source: The slope of the current-voltage relationships for EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 were 3.0 ± 0.18 pS, and 2.9 ± 0.15 pS, respectively, which were not significantly different from KCNQ1 and KCNE1 expressed separately (2.9 ± 0.12 pS; P>0.05).
evidence: This is supported by current-voltage relationship data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The conductances of EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 were not significantly different from KCNQ1 and KCNE1 expressed separately (P>0.05).
source: The slope of the current-voltage relationships for EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 were 3.0 ± 0.18 pS, and 2.9 ± 0.15 pS, respectively, which were not significantly different from KCNQ1 and KCNE1 expressed separately (2.9 ± 0.12 pS; P>0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of current-voltage relationship data.

claim: The mean first latencies to opening of EQQ+KCNE1 was 1.43 ± 0.08 s.
source: The mean first latencies to opening of EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 were now 1.43 ± 0.08 s, and 1.44 ± 0.14 s, respectively, very similar to that reported before for KCNE1+KCNQ1 and measured again here, 1.50 ± 0.12 s.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Table 1.

claim: The mean first latencies to opening of EQQQQ+KCNE1 was 1.44 ± 0.14 s.
source: The mean first latencies to opening of EQQ+KCNE1 and EQQQQ+KCNE1 were now 1.43 ± 0.08 s, and 1.44 ± 0.14 s, respectively, very similar to that reported before for KCNE1+KCNQ1 and measured again here, 1.50 ± 0.12 s.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Table 1.

claim: p-Benzoylphenylalanine (Bpa) can form a covalent crosslink following excitation with UV light (350–380 nm).
source: p-Benzoylphenylalanine (Bpa) can form a covalent crosslink following excitation with UV light (350–380 nm) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the properties of Bpa.

claim: UV light excites the side chain's central ketone of Bpa, generating a triplet oxygen radical.
source: The UV light excites the side chain's central ketone, generating a triplet oxygen radical.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of Bpa crosslinking.

claim: The short-lived radical can abstract a hydrogen atom from a carbon atom within a 3.1-angstrom radius.
source: This short-lived radical can abstract a hydrogen atom from a carbon atom within a 3.1-angstrom radius.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of Bpa crosslinking, supported by a citation.

claim: The resulting alkyl radical then rapidly reacts with the remaining ketyl radical in Bpa to form a covalent bond.
source: The resulting alkyl radical then rapidly reacts with the remaining ketyl radical in Bpa to form a covalent bond (Dorman and Prestwich, 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of Bpa crosslinking, supported by a citation.

claim: Bpa was incorporated into the KCNE1 sequence using the amber stop codon (TAG) suppression system.
source: Bpa was incorporated into the KCNE1 sequence using the amber stop codon (TAG) suppression system (Figure 4A) (Ye et al., 2008; Xie and Schultz, 2005; Young and Schultz, 2010; Chin and Schultz, 2002).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used, supported by citations.

claim: F57 was selected for mutation as it is located within the KCNE1 transmembrane domain and has been previously suggested to interact with KCNQ1 in the channel's closed state.
source: F57 was selected for mutation as it is located within the KCNE1 transmembrane domain and has been previously suggested to interact with KCNQ1 in the channel's closed state although no physical association has been established (Melman et al., 2001; Chen and Goldstein, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: No physical association between F57 and KCNQ1 has been established prior to this study.
source: F57 was selected for mutation as it is located within the KCNE1 transmembrane domain and has been previously suggested to interact with KCNQ1 in the channel's closed state although no physical association has been established (Melman et al., 2001; Chen and Goldstein, 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of prior research.

claim: The M62W KCNE1 mutation has been previously shown not to impact channel gating.
source: The M62W KCNE1 mutation has been previously shown not to impact channel gating, (Chen and Goldstein, 2007) and the same lack of effect was observed here (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research and data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: F57Bpa KCNE1 showed only a 2 mV depolarizing shift in the V1/2 of activation compared to wild type IKs.
source: Plots of tail current G-V relations demonstrated that F57Bpa KCNE1 showed only a 2 mV depolarizing shift in the V1/2 of activation compared to wild type IKs (wild type, 26.1 ± 2.2 mV vs. F57Bpa, 28.2 ± 6.8 mV; n = 3–11) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Incorporation of Bpa at position 57 does not significantly alter expression or channel gating properties.
source: This demonstrates that incorporation of Bpa at position 57 does not significantly alter expression or channel gating properties.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed minimal change in V1/2.

claim: In the absence of Bpa, translation is terminated at the TAG codon, resulting in the expression of a truncated 1–56 β-subunit.
source: In the absence of Bpa, translation is terminated at the TAG codon, resulting in the expression of a truncated 1–56 β-subunit (Figure 4B, lower).
evidence: This is a description of the expected result based on the amber stop codon suppression system.

claim: Currents in the absence of Bpa were similar to KCNQ1 alone.
source: Currents in the absence of Bpa were similar to KCNQ1 alone.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was good fidelity at the TAG site.
source: This indicated that there was good fidelity at the TAG site and that the truncated KCNE1 had no significant impact on the regulation of the channel complex.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that currents without Bpa were similar to KCNQ1 alone.

claim: The truncated KCNE1 had no significant impact on the regulation of the channel complex.
source: This indicated that there was good fidelity at the TAG site and that the truncated KCNE1 had no significant impact on the regulation of the channel complex.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that currents without Bpa were similar to KCNQ1 alone.

claim: In the absence of Bpa, no full-length KCNE1 was observed by Western blot.
source: In the absence of Bpa, no full-length KCNE1 was observed (lanes 2 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Full-length expression of KCNE1-GFP was observed in the presence of Bpa for both the F57TAG KCNE1-Y40TAG GFP and wild type KCNE1-Y40TAG GFP constructs.
source: Full-length expression of KCNE1-GFP was observed in the presence of Bpa for both the F57TAG KCNE1-Y40TAG GFP and wild type KCNE1-Y40TAG GFP constructs indicating good suppression of the amber stop codons by the tRNA and RS.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The application of UV light to F57Bpa channels in the closed state resulted in a rapid and complete loss of peak current.
source: The application of UV light to F57Bpa channels in the closed state resulted in a rapid and complete loss of peak current (Figure 5B-left).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Co-expression of KCNQ1 with wild type KCNE1 exhibited a UV-dependent progressive decline, or rundown, in peak current.
source: Co-expression of KCNQ1 with wild type KCNE1 also exhibited a UV-dependent progressive decline, or rundown, in peak current (Figure 5B-right, open symbols).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The Bpa-specific UV-crosslinking effect was found to be much faster and more complete than the wild type rundown.
source: The Bpa-specific UV-crosslinking effect was found to be much faster and more complete than the wild type rundown (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Western blot analysis indicated a clear increase in the co-association of F57Bpa KCNE1-GFP with KCNQ1 in the presence of longer UV irradiation compared to wild type KCNE1-GFP.
source: Western blot analysis indicated a clear increase in the co-association of F57Bpa KCNE1-GFP with KCNQ1 in the presence of longer UV irradiation compared to wild type KCNE1-GFP.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: F57Bpa forms a UV-dependent covalent crosslink with KCNQ1 that traps the channels in the closed state.
source: These findings, in combination with the UV-current recordings, indicate that F57Bpa forms a UV-dependent covalent crosslink with KCNQ1 that traps the channels in the closed state.
evidence: This is an inference from the UV-crosslinking and co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: UV irradiation of EQQQQ or EQQ co-expressed with F57Bpa KCNE1 resulted in an accelerated rate of peak current decay compared to expression of these constructs with wild type KCNE1-GFP.
source: UV irradiation of EQQQQ or EQQ co-expressed with F57Bpa KCNE1 resulted in an accelerated rate of peak current decay compared to expression of these constructs with wild type KCNE1-GFP (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: F57Bpa can access unoccupied clefts in the EQQQQ and EQQ constructs to allow UV-crosslinking to occur.
source: The results clearly suggest that F57Bpa can access unoccupied clefts in the EQQQQ and EQ constructs to allow UV-crosslinking to occur.
evidence: This is an inference from the UV-crosslinking data.

claim: UV-treatment of EQ co-expressed with F57Bpa KCNE1 did not cause any crosslinking-dependent current decrease compared to EQ co-expressed with wild type KCNE1.
source: UV-treatment did not cause any crosslinking-dependent current decrease compared to EQ co-expressed with wild type KCNE1 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: There is minimal displacement of the tethered β-subunits in a voltage sensor cleft by an independent one.
source: This finding indicates that there is minimal displacement of the tethered β-subunits in a voltage sensor cleft by an independent one.
evidence: This is an inference from the UV-crosslinking data for EQ.

claim: More rapid F57Bpa KCNE1 crosslinking occurs as the number of potentially available clefts increases.
source: Analysis of the fast rate constants revealed more rapid F57Bpa KCNE1 crosslinking as the number of potentially available clefts increased (EQQ – 2 clefts, 0.55 ± 0.06 s-1; EQQQQ – 3 clefts, 0.63 ± 0.06 s-1; KCNQ1 – 4 clefts, 1.12 ± 0.09 s-1 (n = 5–7)) (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of UV-crosslinking rate constants shown in Figure 5G.

claim: More F57Bpa KCNE1-GFP subunits are interacting with the KCNQ1 channel complexes, as more clefts are available.
source: These findings demonstrate that more F57Bpa KCNE1-GFP subunits are interacting with the KCNQ1 channel complexes, as more clefts are available.
evidence: This is an inference from the UV-crosslinking rate data.

claim: EQ + F57Bpa had a UV decay rate no different than the rundown observed for all wild type channels.
source: EQ, which has no available clefts, had a UV decay rate no different than the rundown observed for all wild type channels, and significantly slower than other channel configurations (KXL: EQ + F57Bpa, 0.09 ± 0.09 s-1: p<0.01 (n = 5), Figure 5G).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of UV-crosslinking rate constants shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The intermediate rates of crosslinking for EQQQQ and EQQ between KCNQ1 and EQ indicate that F57Bpa KCNE1 can access the unoccupied clefts in the channel complexes.
source: The intermediate rates of crosslinking for EQQQQ and EQQ between KCNQ1 and EQ indicate that F57Bpa KCNE1 can access the unoccupied clefts in the channel complexes.
evidence: This is an inference from the UV-crosslinking rate data.

claim: There is no intrinsic restriction of β-subunit association.
source: These findings demonstrate that there is no intrinsic restriction of β-subunit association and confirms a variable stoichiometry model for IKs channel complex composition.
evidence: This is an inference from the UV-crosslinking data.

claim: Up to four KCNE1's can interact per KCNQ1 tetramer.
source: Using these approaches we were able to determine that up to four KCNE1's can interact per KCNQ1 tetramer.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by all the experimental data.

claim: EQQQQ and EQQ have a hyperpolarized voltage dependence of activation compared to EQ or wild type IKs.
source: Whole cell patch clamp studies indicated that EQQQQ and EQQ have a hyperpolarized voltage dependence of activation compared to EQ or wild type IKs, which could be normalized by co-expression of additional KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by whole cell patch clamp data.

claim: The hyperpolarized voltage dependence of activation of EQQQQ and EQQ could be normalized by co-expression of additional KCNE1.
source: Whole cell patch clamp studies indicated that EQQQQ and EQQ have a hyperpolarized voltage dependence of activation compared to EQ or wild type IKs, which could be normalized by co-expression of additional KCNE1.
evidence: This is supported by whole cell patch clamp data.

claim: EQQQQ and EQQ had a shorter first latency to open at +60 mV compared with wild type.
source: We also observed the same phenomenon in single channels, where EQQQQ and EQQ had a shorter first latency to open and reduced conductance that equaled EQ and wild type IKs channels when KCNE1 was co-transfected.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data.

claim: EQQQQ and EQQ had reduced conductance that equaled EQ and wild type IKs channels when KCNE1 was co-transfected.
source: We also observed the same phenomenon in single channels, where EQQQQ and EQQ had a shorter first latency to open and reduced conductance that equaled EQ and wild type IKs channels when KCNE1 was co-transfected.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data.

claim: KCNE1 can incorporate into the EQQQQ and EQQ channel complexes.
source: Finally, our key experiment using a photo-crosslinking unnatural amino acid, unequivocally demonstrated that KCNE1 can incorporate into the EQQQQ and EQQ channel complexes.
evidence: This is supported by UV-crosslinking data.

claim: Up to four KCNE1 subunits can regulate KCNQ1.
source: Taken together, our findings verify that up to four KCNE1 subunits can regulate KCNQ1.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by all the experimental data.

claim: Several previous studies support the finding that the ratio is variable ranging from 1–4 KCNE1's depending on their availability.
source: As summarized in the Introduction, several previous studies support these findings, in suggesting that the ratio is variable ranging from 1–4 KCNE1's depending on their availability.
evidence: This is a summary of prior research.

claim: The debate has recently coalesced around an opposing idea that IKs has a strict 2:4 ratio of KCNE1's:KCNQ1's.
source: However, this debate has recently coalesced around an opposing idea that IKs has a strict 2:4 ratio of KCNE1's:KCNQ1's (Kang et al., 2008; Morin and Kobertz, 2008; Plant et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a summary of prior research.

claim: An independently expressed KCNE1 can associate with EQQ, so that a stoichiometry greater than 2:4 is possible.
source: We clearly show that an independently expressed KCNE1 can associate with EQQ, so that a stoichiometry greater than 2:4 is possible, and indeed that there is no intrinsic mechanism limiting the association of KCNE1 with the channel complex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: There is no intrinsic mechanism limiting the association of KCNE1 with the channel complex.
source: We clearly show that an independently expressed KCNE1 can associate with EQQ, so that a stoichiometry greater than 2:4 is possible, and indeed that there is no intrinsic mechanism limiting the association of KCNE1 with the channel complex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: The V1/2's of the current-voltage relationships for KCNQ1 alone, EQQQQ, EQQ, and EQ, increased linearly with increasing KCNE1 presence.
source: The V1/2's of the current-voltage relationships for KCNQ1 alone, EQQQQ, EQQ, and EQ, increased linearly with increasing KCNE1 presence (Figure 6), as can also be observed using the data presented by Yu et al. (2013).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6 and a citation to prior research.

claim: Each β-subunit that associates appears to have a similar contribution in regulating the midpoint of the voltage dependence of activation.
source: Each β-subunit that associates appears to have a similar contribution in regulating the midpoint of the voltage dependence of activation, and the linear change in the V1/2 does not support cooperative gating effects of additional KCNE1 association.
evidence: This is an inference from the linear relationship observed in Figure 6.

claim: The linear change in the V1/2 does not support cooperative gating effects of additional KCNE1 association.
source: Each β-subunit that associates appears to have a similar contribution in regulating the midpoint of the voltage dependence of activation, and the linear change in the V1/2 does not support cooperative gating effects of additional KCNE1 association.
evidence: This is an inference from the linear relationship observed in Figure 6.

claim: Residue F57 in KCNE1 interacts with KCNQ1 in the resting state in a conformation that prevents channel opening.
source: The results of our crosslinking study also implicate KCNE1 in regulating the pore domain by showing that residue F57 in KCNE1 interacts with KCNQ1 in the resting state in a conformation that prevents channel opening (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an inference from the UV-crosslinking data shown in Figure 5.

claim: F57 has been identified as part of the 'activation triplet' consisting of F57, T58 and L59, which has been found to interact with the pore region of the channel.
source: F57 has been identified as part of the 'activation triplet' consisting of F57, T58 and L59, which has been found to interact with the pore region of the channel (Wang et al., 1996; Tapper and George, 2001; Melman et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A crosslinking event between KCNE1 and the pore region could restrict its movement and prevent channel opening.
source: A crosslinking event between KCNE1 and the pore region could restrict its movement and prevent channel opening.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of crosslinking.

claim: KCNE1 inhibits the movement of the S4 domain in the voltage sensor.
source: There are several theories for how KCNE1 delays channel opening, including that KCNE1 inhibits the movement of the S4 domain in the voltage sensor, (Nakajo and Kubo, 2007; Ruscic et al., 2013) or that it slows the opening of the pore domain (Rocheleau and Kobertz, 2008; Osteen et al., 2010; Barro-Soria et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: KCNE1 slows the opening of the pore domain.
source: There are several theories for how KCNE1 delays channel opening, including that KCNE1 inhibits the movement of the S4 domain in the voltage sensor, (Nakajo and Kubo, 2007; Ruscic et al., 2013) or that it slows the opening of the pore domain (Rocheleau and Kobertz, 2008; Osteen et al., 2010; Barro-Soria et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Zaydman et al. (2014) propose that KCNE1 does not directly affect VSD activation or pore opening, and instead suggest that KCNE1 alters the state-dependent interactions linking the VSD and pore in KCNQ1 channels.
source: Our findings suggesting that KCNE1 potentially impacts both are supported by a recent paper by Zaydman et al. (2014). They propose that KCNE1 does not directly affect VSD activation or pore opening, and instead suggest that KCNE1 alters the state-dependent interactions linking the VSD and pore in KCNQ1 channels.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: If KCNE1 affects the interactions between the two domains, it is plausible that KCNE1 not only independently modulates the voltage dependence of its own α-subunit, but also participates in interactions that, when covalently crosslinked, can prevent channel opening.
source: If KCNE1 affects the interactions between the two domains, it is plausible that KCNE1 not only independently modulates the voltage dependence of its own α-subunit, but also participates in interactions that, when covalently crosslinked, can prevent channel opening.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the Zaydman et al. model and the crosslinking data.

claim: EQQ and EQQQQ channels had a reduced first latency to open at +60 mV compared with wild type.
source: In addition to a hyperpolarizing shift in V1/2 (Figure 1), our single channel analysis indicated that EQQ and EQQQQ channels had a reduced first latency to open at +60 mV compared with wild type (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Table 1.

claim: Unsaturated channels rarely reach a fully conducting state, and instead they primarily reside in subconducting conformations.
source: Also, unsaturated channels rarely reach a fully conducting state, and instead they primarily reside in subconducting conformations (Figures 2, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data shown in Figures 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The modulation of both first latency and conductance is consistent with the kind of regulatory model proposed by Zaydman et al. (2014), in which KCNQ1 has intermediate and activated voltage sensor states, both of which lead to channel opening, but where KCNE1 suppresses opening in the intermediate state.
source: The modulation of both these parameters is consistent with the kind of regulatory model proposed by Zaydman et al. (2014), in which KCNQ1 has intermediate and activated voltage sensor states, both of which lead to channel opening, but where KCNE1 suppresses opening in the intermediate state.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the experimental data to a prior model.

claim: EQQ and EQQQQ would represent hybrid channels; QQ subunits lacking E1 could open from an earlier gating state while those associated with E1 open from a more fully activated state.
source: In this scenario, EQQ and EQQQQ would represent hybrid channels; QQ subunits lacking E1 could open from an earlier gating state while those associated with E1 open from a more fully activated state.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism based on the Zaydman et al. model.

claim: Wild type channels show a mean conductance of 3.2 pS and also exhibit several sub-conducting levels.
source: We have previously observed that wild type channels show a mean conductance of 3.2 pS and also exhibit several sub-conducting levels (Werry et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: KCNQ1 is thought to have a reduced channel conductance.
source: On its own, KCNQ1 is thought to have a reduced channel conductance, although this has not been confirmed by single channel analysis (Yang and Sigworth, 1998; Pusch, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research, but noted as not confirmed by single-channel analysis.

claim: In the presence of only two KCNE1 subunits, the pore is still capable of achieving a wild type conducting state, but much less frequently such that a mean conductance of ~1.3 pS was observed.
source: Our findings indicate that in the presence of only two KCNE1 subunits, the pore is still capable of achieving a wild type conducting state, but much less frequently such that a mean conductance of ~1.3 pS was observed.
evidence: This is supported by single-channel data.

claim: In the presence of only one E1 subunit (EQQQQ) the effect was even greater and points to a destabilized open pore configuration in the absence of KCNE1.
source: In the presence of only one E1 subunit (EQQQQ) the effect was even greater and points to a destabilized open pore configuration in the absence of KCNE1.
evidence: This is an inference from the single-channel data.

claim: This is the first direct demonstration that sub-saturating levels of KCNE1 lowers mean single channel conductance.
source: Others have reported that KCNE1 can interact and modulate the characteristics of the pore domain but this is the first direct demonstration that sub-saturating levels of KCNE1 lowers mean single channel conductance, and it indicates that 4 KCNE1's preferentially stabilize the ion throughput rate of the open pore (Wang et al., 1996; Tapper and George, 2001; Melman et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, supported by data and citations.

claim: 4 KCNE1's preferentially stabilize the ion throughput rate of the open pore.
source: Others have reported that KCNE1 can interact and modulate the characteristics of the pore domain but this is the first direct demonstration that sub-saturating levels of KCNE1 lowers mean single channel conductance, and it indicates that 4 KCNE1's preferentially stabilize the ion throughput rate of the open pore (Wang et al., 1996; Tapper and George, 2001; Melman et al., 2004).
evidence: This is an inference from the single-channel data.

claim: A full complement of KCNE1 enhances KCNQ1 channel activity.
source: These findings indicate that a full complement of KCNE1 enhances KCNQ1 channel activity.
evidence: This is an inference from the single-channel data.

claim: A characterization of IKs currents in dog cardiac myocytes determined the V1/2 at 37°C for IKs across different regions of the ventricular wall to be ~25 mV.
source: A characterization of IKs currents in dog cardiac myocytes determined the V1/2 at 37°C for IKs across different regions of the ventricular wall to be ~25 mV (Liu and Antzelevitch, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Co-localization studies of KCNE1 and KCNQ1 in rat cardiomyocytes indicated that KCNE1 is present in excess.
source: Additionally, co-localization studies of KCNE1 and KCNQ1 in rat cardiomyocytes indicated that KCNE1 is present in excess (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Under conditions where KCNE1 is present in excess, it is likely that many of the IKs channel complexes have a β-subunits configuration exceeding 2:4.
source: Our results and these previous findings suggest that under these conditions, it is likely that many of the IKs channel complexes have a β-subunits configuration exceeding 2:4.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data and prior research.

claim: A fully saturated channel has a depolarizing shift in the current-voltage relationship, extremely slowed activation and increased conductance.
source: A fully saturated channel has a depolarizing shift in the current-voltage relationship, extremely slowed activation and increased conductance (Figure 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: During a normal cardiac action potential a fully saturated channel would result in limited activation.
source: However, during a normal cardiac action potential this would result in limited activation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the properties of fully saturated channels.

claim: If the stoichiometry can be regulated based on availability, then altering the expression could change the distribution of channel composition, shifting the overall activation kinetics of the current.
source: If the stoichiometry can be regulated based on availability, (Nakajo et al., 2010) then altering the expression could change the distribution of channel composition, shifting the overall activation kinetics of the current.
evidence: This is a speculation about the physiological implications, supported by a citation.

claim: All five of the KCNE genes (KCNE1-5) can be expressed in cardiomyocytes.
source: Additionally, there is evidence for the association of other β-subunits. All five of the KCNE genes (KCNE1-5) can be expressed in cardiomyocytes (Lundquist et al., 2006; Bendahhou et al., 2005; Radicke et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Each of the KCNE accessory proteins has been found to alter KCNQ1 channel gating in distinct ways.
source: Each of these accessory proteins has been found to alter KCNQ1 channel gating in distinct ways (Eldstrom and Fedida, 2011; Liin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There is potential for different KCNE's associating with the same channel to modulate its function.
source: There is also potential for different KCNE's associating with the same channel to modulate its function (Manderfield and George, 2008; Jiang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Flexibility in KCNQ1's β-subunits association, both in number and in type, allows for a powerful mechanism to modulate repolarization in the heart through changes in expression.
source: Flexibility in KCNQ1's β-subunits association, both in number and in type, allows for a powerful mechanism to modulate repolarization in the heart through changes in expression.
evidence: This is a speculation about the physiological implications.

claim: Variable association allows for greater flexibility in the modulation of IKs current but also potentially increases the heterogeneity of channel species in the membrane.
source: Variable association allows for greater flexibility in the modulation of IKs current but also potentially increases the heterogeneity of channel species in the membrane.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of variable stoichiometry.
